company_overview: Designs and manufactures high-performance computing servers, workstations, and storage systems for enterprise and govt clients
Revenue model: project-based B2B supply, with servicing and AMC as recurring stream (~10% of revenue)
Key segments: HPC servers (55%), enterprise storage (25%), workstations (20%)
Market position: #2 domestic server OEM by revenue; competes with Dell, HPE on price
Promoter: Sanjay Lodha group, ~52% promoter holding, no pledge
Geography: 95% domestic, 5% exports (targeting 15% exports in 3 years)
Key clients: BFSI, defence PSUs, central govt ministries — top 3 = 45% revenue
Regulatory: empanelled with MeitY for govt procurement — protects from direct foreign competition
Revenue CAGR 3Y: ~65%; PAT CAGR 3Y: ~80% — highest growth phase in company history
Moat: MeitY empanelment + govt procurement preference for domestic OEMs; switching cost low on product but high on govt relationship
concall.one_liner: Data centre demand driving 40%+ growth with strong order book visibility into FY26.
guidance: Revenue FY26: 1800 Cr guided (~40% growth on FY25 base of ~1280 Cr)
EBITDA margin: 14-15% maintained (FY25 delivered 14.2%)
Order book: 1800 Cr executable over 12 months as of Q4 call
Capex FY26: 80-100 Cr for facility expansion at Nalagarh
Hyperscale segment launch: first revenue expected H2 FY26
Export target: 150-200 Cr in FY26 (currently negligible)
No dividend guidance; reinvesting all FCF into capacity
Headcount: adding 200 engineers in FY26 for GPU server assembly
Working capital target: maintain ~90 days (currently 92 days)
Milestone: GPU server assembly certification from 2 global OEMs by Q2 FY26
strategic_updates: Entering hyperscale data centre segment — targeting cloud providers and large enterprises
JV with Taiwanese ODM for GPU server assembly under MeitY procurement
Capacity expansion at Nalagarh to 2x current capacity by Q3 FY26
New product: liquid cooling solutions for high-density AI compute racks
Won 3 new defence PSU contracts worth ~280 Cr in Q4
Targeting US export certification for workstations (filing by Q1 FY26)
Cost optimisation: component localisation reducing BOM cost by 8%
New CTO hired from global OEM — first external senior hire in 5 years
earnings_triggers: First hyperscale order win above 200 Cr — would confirm addressable market expansion
Capacity utilisation crossing 80% — signals operating leverage inflection
Export revenue hitting 5% of total — de-risks govt concentration
GPU assembly line certification — unlocks AI infra demand
Any index inclusion (Nifty Midcap 150 threshold at current mcap)
Analyst coverage initiation by top brokerage (currently covered by 3 small brokers only)
Promoter open market buying — last bought in Oct 2024
Q result beat vs street estimates by more than 10%
Margin expansion above 15% EBITDA — not yet guided
Strategic partner announcement for overseas distribution
risks: Dependent on govt and BFSI spending — both can delay in election year or budget cuts
Customer concentration: top 3 = 45% revenue — single cancellation hits badly
Component lead times elevated for high-end GPUs (NVIDIA allocations constrained)
No pricing power vs Dell/HPE in open commercial market — wins only on govt preference
Execution risk: hyperscale is new segment — management has no prior track record here
FX risk if imports rise significantly (currently 40% of COGS imported)
Debt-free now but capex expansion may require external funding in FY27
Valuation (42x PE) — any demand slowdown compresses multiple sharply
No promoter pledge but promoter selling 2% stake in QIP diluted FY25
Regulatory: MeitY empanelment can be revoked if compliance lapses

qa.q: Can margins sustain at 14%+ with hyperscale?
qa.a: Yes, hyperscale margins are higher — we target 16-17% EBITDA on those contracts

qa.q: Order book concentration — any single order above 20% of backlog?
qa.a: No, largest single order is 12% of current backlog

qa.q: Risk of order cancellation in backlog?
qa.a: All backed by purchase orders with penalties, no historical cancellations

qa.q: GPU availability — can you meet FY26 targets?
qa.a: We have allocation commitments from 2 distributors covering 70% of our FY26 GPU needs

qa.q: Why not paying dividend given zero debt?
qa.a: We see 3-4x better return reinvesting in capacity versus paying dividend at current growth stage

qa.q: What is the hyperscale pipeline size?
qa.a: Management deflected — said pipeline is robust but would not quantify. Watch for this.

consistency.promise: Q2: order book 1400 Cr by Q4

consistency.actual: 58 Cr spent — slight underspend on timing

concall.credibility_label: Beats own guidance consistently — 4 straight quarter beats
concall.investor_verdict: Management is conservative and consistently delivers or beats guidance. Business is in structural tailwind from AI infra and data centre buildout in India. Key risk is valuation at 42x PE — any demand slowdown or guidance cut would compress the multiple sharply. Hyperscale ambition is exciting but unproven — track Q1 FY26 for first data points. Would trust this team with capital.

action.label: STRONG HOLD
action.rationale: Strong Stage 2B, management credible (5 stars), earnings accelerating 4 consecutive quarters. Add only on 8-10% dip to 50MA (3620). Do not chase at 52W high proximity.

company_overview: Kirloskar Engines India manufactures diesel and gas engines for industrial, marine, and power generation applications
Revenue model: product sales (70%) + spares and services (30% — high margin recurring)
Market leader in medium-speed diesel engines in India with ~40% market share
Strong promoter family (Kirloskar group), ~55% holding, zero pledge
Benefits from PLI for capital goods and defence indigenisation push
3Y revenue CAGR ~15%, PAT CAGR ~25% — margin expansion phase
concall.one_liner: Export order wins accelerating with industrial recovery — margin expansion from spares mix continuing.
guidance: Revenue FY26: 4200-4500 Cr (15-18% growth)
EBITDA margin: 14-15% target (vs 13.2% in FY25)
Export revenue: 800 Cr target (vs 620 Cr FY25)
Capex: 150-180 Cr for capacity expansion
strategic_updates: New gas engine product line for CNG gensets — addresses energy transition
Defence order pipeline: 3 active tenders for naval vessels
Spares distribution network expanded to 180 service centres (from 140)
earnings_triggers: Gas engine product launch revenue hitting 200 Cr
Margin crossing 15% EBITDA — operating leverage from utilisation
Index inclusion in Nifty 500 (close to threshold)
risks: Diesel engine demand at risk from EV/electric transition over 5-10 year horizon
Input cost (steel, copper) exposure if commodity cycle turns
Export growth depends on global capex — can slow in recession
Customer concentration in industrial/infra — govt spending slowdown risk

qa.q: EV risk to diesel engine business?
qa.a: Diesel engines have 10+ year runway in industrial and defence — no risk in our planning horizon

qa.q: When does gas engine business become material?
qa.a: Expect 15% of revenue by FY27 — currently 5%

concall.credibility_label: Reliable — mostly on track with conservative guidance
concall.investor_verdict: Kirloskar Engines is a quality compounder in the industrial capex cycle. Strong moat (market share, spares network), improving margins, and export growth give multiple expansion runway. Near 52W high but earnings justify current valuation at 28x PE — below the sector mean of 32x. Best momentum stock in the portfolio.

action.label: STRONG ADD
action.rationale: Best momentum + fundamentals combo in portfolio. Score 88/100. Add on any 5-8% dip to 50MA (1090). Maximum weight 20% given strong thesis.

company_overview: Bajaj Holdings is a NBFC investment company holding stakes in Bajaj Finance, Bajaj Finserv, and other Bajaj group companies
Not an operating company — revenue = dividend income + investment gains from subsidiaries
Structural HoldCo discount: market cap is ~35% below NAV of listed holdings
Promoter: Rahul Bajaj family, ~55% holding, zero pledge
Key holding: Bajaj Finance (33% stake, most valuable); Bajaj Finserv (39% stake)
concall.one_liner: HoldCo discount widened as Bajaj Finance growth concerns weigh — no near-term catalyst to close the gap.
guidance: No operating guidance — holding company structure
NAV as of Q4: ~17,200 per share (vs CMP 11,240 = 35% discount)
Dividend: maintained at 160 per share
strategic_updates: Continuing to hold core stakes — no monetisation plans mentioned
earnings_triggers: Bajaj Finance re-rating if RBI removes regulatory embargo
HoldCo discount narrowing if market re-rates the structure
risks: Bajaj Finance faces regulatory headwinds (RBI scrutiny on unsecured lending)
HoldCo discount can persist or widen in risk-off markets
No operating leverage — pure pass-through of subsidiary performance
NBFC sector facing margin compression from rising cost of funds

qa.q: Any plans to close the HoldCo discount?
qa.a: Management acknowledged the discount but said no immediate structural change planned
Redirected to Bajaj Finance's own management commentary

concall.credibility_label: Limited — holding company with minimal direct management actions
concall.investor_verdict: Bajaj Holdings is a quality asset at a structural discount but with no near-term catalyst to close it. The Stage 3 technical setup and slowing subsidiary earnings (Bajaj Finance headwinds) make this a watch-and-wait situation. Trim 50% if price fails to recover above 11,800 in 4-6 weeks. The thesis is intact long-term but position sizing should reflect the technical risk.

action.label: WATCH
action.rationale: Score 52/100 — solid business but Stage 3 and slowing earnings. Hold current position. Trim 50% (to ~4%) if no recovery above 11,800 by end of June 2026.
